To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bamboo species growing at high altitude are found to have low level of TCG and rich in nutritious attributes.
edible bamboo species of North-East India are rich in TCC, low in antioxidant properties, and have low levels of beneficial nutrients.

the edible bamboo species with large bamboo-shoot texture growing at low altitude are found to be rich in total cyanogenic content irrespective of the growing region and season, whereas edible bamboo species with small bamboo-shoot texture grown at high altitude are found to have low total cyanogenic content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of safe edible bamboo species for consumer safety and for the conservation of gene pool.
the identification of safe and nutritious edible bamboo species with high altitude for the development of bamboo-based products and to avoid food poisoning.
the development of a comprehensive database for the characterization of edible bamboo shoots for safe consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the edible bamboo species with high nutritious attributes and low cyanogenic content can be found at high altitude.
edible bamboo species with large and robust bamboo shoots and growing at low altitudes contain high level of total CN content and toxic cyanide and should be consumed with caution.
the edible bamboo shoots with high level of TCG and low level of beneficial macronitrients and micronutrient are not suitable for human consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, edible bamboo species with high nutritious attributes and low TCC can be found in the high altitudes of north-east India.
edible bamboo species with high nutritious attributes and low TCC can be obtained from the high altitude.
, edible bamboo species having low altitude and high TCC are not safe for human consumption and the species having high altitude and low TCC are safe for human consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bamboo species with large bamboo-shoot size, growing at low altitude, are not safe for consumption due to high level of cyanogenic compounds and poor nutritional attributes.
the edible bamboo species growing at high altitude are safe for human consumption with low TCC and rich in macronutrients, and hence, should be promoted to the consumers.

the edible bamboo species with high nutritious attributes and low level of TBC are found to grow at high altitudes, which is contrary to the popular notion of edible bamboo species growing at low altitude.
